chunk_map.heading: # Map the gaps, read your stack (title + lede)
## Phase 1: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps
## Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
## Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
## Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule
## Phase 2: Find the work you repeat across your stack
## Scan your history for the work that recurs
## Draw your top work-shapes as diagrams
## Sidestep: check your menu against the field's
## Decide what crosses back to your main repo

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Traced every pronoun/demonstrative/label across all 10 chunks in order. 'M4'/'M5'/'M6' shorthand (chunk 0-1) resolve via arc-earned spine vocabulary (module names carve-out, §1). 'the packaging' / 'the quote rule' (chunk 2) resolve against the four-dimension prompt read in chunk 1 (same-file, prior chunk). 'the dominant gap' (chunk 5) resolves against chunk 2's close ('a dominant gap that shapes the rest of this phase'). 'handoff prompt' (chunk 8, line 142 'What happened') is never defined inside this exercise file, but the enclosing module file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md line 19 names it in its What You'll Learn bullet ('Generalize the shapes you mapped into a handoff prompt...') — module include-order carve-out (§1) makes it prior context for the exercise it includes. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

grep -n '\[.*\](' curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md → no output. Body carries zero markdown links, so no cross-file positional pointer exists to evaluate. Session-artifact references to 'the M5 worktree' / 'M5's packaging' name the prior module by number, not by page position, and fall under the module-arc carve-out in §1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for '(the X) you (did|saw|caught|ran|built|wrote|read|named)' → no hits in body. The file's backward pointers (M4 un-packaged session / M5 packaged re-send, task.md, plan.md) were checked against curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md (the module file), which confirms M4 and M5 are real prior modules with matching artefacts ('diff un-packaged M4 vs packaged M5', 'M5 worktree', task.md/plan.md coordinates cited at module lines 116-118, 132). No dangling beat reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body — this exercise is a diff-and-diagnose task, not a live-demo beat with a narrated outcome.

Closest candidate is chunk 4 ('Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule', lines 69-72): two bullets, but each carries a standalone instruction (reassure on the config-file pause; cap the diff to one rule) rather than a bare wait-state. Every other chunk carries a prompt, a multi-bullet setup, or a substantive callout. No chunk is content-free.

Checked all 9 '##' headers against their chunk content: 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' → chunk body cuts a stale rule; 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' → chunk body is exactly that guardrail; 'Sidestep: check your menu against the field's' → chunk compares the student's primitives against a field-sourced list. No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all sub-items across body: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction found; no anaphora/epistrophe triples found; no self-grading superlative ('one of the most useful...') found — closest is chunk 0's 'two runs are enough to place every lesson', which is a claim about the method, not self-grading praise of this exercise; no number-with-retraction pattern found (no bare percentages/counts in body prose); no abstraction-noun stack found; no empty-leg verb triplet found. All sub-items PASS, including the blocking self-grading-superlative sub-item.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned body for maintainer-dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections). None appear in body. 'Packaging' and 'verifier' are AE101 taught vocabulary from M5 (curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md), not repo-internal authoring jargon — student-facing, arc-earned terms, not dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep '\*\*[^*]*\*\*' over the raw body (lines 3-101, before maintainer cut) → every bold span is a short handle (≤5 words: 'Time:', 'Session', 'What you do:', 'What you build:', 'The point:', 'Fast operator?', 'Cut the scan...', 'Want to see the shapes...', 'What happened:', 'Note'), each followed by unbolded prose — no whole-sentence bolded leads. Maintainer block itself confirms an emphasis pass already de-bolded bullet leads to plain (2026-07-09 note, line 99 of raw file). Budget holds at ≤1 handle per chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is a standard curriculum/exercises/ file, composed into the M6 module via the ordinary exercise include path (a `.phase--exercise` wrapper per training-architecture.md), not a phase-less prework/supplementary-shaped section — the failure mode this rule guards against (2026-07-09 prework/supplementary drop). No basis to suspect deck-absence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` → "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." Phase 1 / Phase 2 are consecutive from 1, no hand-numbered header for slide position, no stray in-file Phase/Step reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` → "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." grep -iE '(above|below|further down|at the top of this|see below|this page)' over the body also returned zero hits (the one 'below' hit, 'Whole-room mood below 7', sits past the maintainer cut and is a numeric threshold, not a page pointer). The chunk-6 'Fast operator?' callout's 'the next two prompts' is a reading-order pointer (sequence-preserving), not a page-position one — allowed under this rule's own fallback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -n '\[.*\](' curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md → no output. Zero in-body links in this file, nothing to evaluate for this review-only, never-gating rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md` → "files: 1  slides: 9  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets\noversized: 0\n✓ every slide is within limits". No accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 9 body '##' headers checked: 'Phase 1: Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' / 'Phase 2: ...' are phase labels; 'Read the contrast...', 'Cut one stale rule...', 'Say go, unless...', 'Scan your history...', 'Draw your top work-shapes...', 'Sidestep: check your menu...', 'Decide what crosses back...' are all imperatives. Zero declarative-claim headers — consistent with this exercise not being one of the two declaratives the compendium's 2026-08-15 corpus measurement names (close-the-ticket.md, fix-tests-first.md).

notes: Only check_slides.md carries eval_classes: slides in its frontmatter among the 12 check_*.md compendiums under memory/ — confirmed by inspecting each file's metadata.eval_classes list directly (the earlier attempt with a bare-line grep on 'eval_classes:' returned false negatives because the key sits nested under a 'metadata:' block with 2-space indent and the list items use 4-space indent). check_writing.md's §14/§15/§18 sibling rules generalize into this compendium's rules 1/3/6 per the compendium's own cross-references and were not separately re-scored here, per the dispatch preamble's lane discipline. The chunk-6 'Fast operator?' forward pointer to 'the next two prompts' was considered as a possible §1/§12 issue and resolved as an allowed reading-order pointer, not filed.
